recipes.name: To-Die-For Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 cup fresh or frozen green beans, thawed
4 (.87 ounce) packages dry chicken gravy mix
1 (15 ounce) package double crust ready-to-use pie crusts (such as Pillsbury®)
1 whole roasted chicken, bones and skin removed, meat shredded

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Place a baking sheet on the a rack on which you’ll bake the pie.

Combine the carrots, celery, peas, green beans, corn, onion, red potatoes, and chicken broth in a large pot. Season the vegetable mixture with thyme, salt, and black pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes. Drain the vegetables and set aside.

Place dry chicken gravy mix into another saucepan and gradually whisk in the water until smooth. Bring the mixture to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until thickened, about 1 minute. Set gravy aside and allow to continue to thicken as it cools.

Press one of the pie crusts into the bottom of a 9-inch pie dish. Spoon a layer of gravy (about 1/3 cup) into the crust. Layer the cooked vegetables and shredded chicken into the crust until the filling is level with the top of the pie dish. Pour the rest of the gravy slowly over the filling until gravy is visible at the top. Scatter butter pieces over the filling; top with second crust. Seal the 2 crusts together and crimp with a fork.
Whisk the egg and milk together in a bowl, and brush the egg wash over the top crust. Pierce the top crust several times to vent steam.

Bake the pot pie in the preheated oven until the filling is bubbling and the crust is golden brown, about 45 minutes to 1 hour. Check periodically to see if the edge of the crust is browning too quickly; if needed, cover the edge with a strip of aluminum foil to prevent over-browning.

raw_recipe.headline: To-Die-For Chicken Pot Pie
raw_recipe.description: Using premade pie crust, gravy mix, and a store-bought rotisserie chicken cuts a lot of steps from this comforting chicken pot pie. This recipe is crammed with vegetables and chicken and makes a lot of filling, maybe even enough for 2 pies or several smaller pies.

video.description: This is a recipe passed down from my Mom. Every time I make it, someone asks for the recipe. One friend says her family fights over it! I hope you enjoy it! You can also make a homemade chicken soup with this recipe.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic recipe. Used 2 lb chicken breast, coated in thyme, rosemary, and basil then topped with butter pats and baked. Fork shredded the chicken, which distributed the spices throughout all the meat. Aside from that, followed the recipe as written. Would possibly add a little more gravy and add it in layers along with the filling, the filling was too dense for it to filter through so the bottom and top only had gravy. Finally, best in a deep dish pie pan. Everyone at home and at work raved about this recipe. You won't be disappointed.

Delicious! My husband actually made this one and he's not the best cook and it still turned out wonderful! He did cook the veggies for a lot longer than 15 minutes but that was the only change he made

I cut all quantities in 1/2 except seasonings. Omitted the 4 cups of water. After just one read of the recipe, I realized it all would never fit in one pie tin. I used a bag frozen mixed veggies, fresh 1/2 chopped onion, minced garlic clove, rough cut 3 medium golden potatoes & 3 stalks celery. I boiled them in 3-4 cups of chicken broth (with the seasonings) for about 6-8 minutes. Drained & saved 2 cups of the broth. I used 1 packet of dry 2.75 oz Pioneer Country Gravy mix & 2 cups of the saved broth, and chopped breast & thighs of a rotisserie chicken. I also baked the bottom crust for about 5-8 minutes before putting the bottom layer of gravy. My husband says it’s the best thing I’ve made in ages! Just the 2 of us so I just reheat it at 300deg F, cover with foil, bake for 20-25. Perfecto!

This was a great recipe. Followed the recipe w/ one small change - instead of using water w/ the chicken gravy, I used some of the chicken broth the veggies cooked in. It didn't get as thick as I would've preferred it. Regardless very good recipe!

Great recipe. I used a 3" deep casserole dish and doubled the pie crust. Also did not use water...cooked all in low-sodium chicken broth. If you do this, be careful how much extra salt you add. Also used 2 packages of chicken gravy and 2 mushroom gravy and added some mushrooms rather than the corn. Lastly I only cooked it for about 30min or the crust would have burned. Since all is cooked going in, the only reason it goes in the oven is to bake the piecrust. YUM!!!

To be fair, I didn’t really follow this recipe as written, but the proportions and method are good. I made my own crust and gravy instead of store-bought, and I sautéed all veggies except for potatoes instead of boiling. I added sage to the thyme for seasoning. This recipe is now a regular in my house. Even my picky son likes it. It’s easy and very good. My only suggestion is to use a deep dish pie shell/pan. I don’t know how this volume of ingredients could fit in a regular 9” pie dish. I used a 10” cast iron deep skillet.

Made this over the weekend. WOW. Definitely a keeper And a sharer! Used a can each of Cream of Chicken and Cream of Mushroom soup mixed with about 1/2C half&half. Included a small can of mushroom pieces(drained), a bag of frozen mixed veggies, and a few, fresh small potatoes (quartered). Didn’t have thyme, so I substituted 1/2tsp of poultry seasoning. Mixed it all and added salt/ pepper to taste. Poured on top of my pre-baked bottom crust, added the top crust, covered the crust edges and baked as instructed. Since it was all I had on hand, I used frozen PUFF PASTRY dough, not Pie Crust. Although the bottom puffed when I pre-baked, I just pushed it all down into the pie plate. The bottom crust turned out crispy, as was the top which really made the pie super yummy. We all had second helpings!

I made this using Costco rotisserie chicken that is already deboned and sold in 3 lb packages. Also, made my own gravy - rue from butter and flour, used broth from cooked vegetables, added some more chicken broth and a teaspoon of Better Than Bullion with salt and pepper to taste. I used a deep casserole dish instead of pie pan. Glad I did since the quantity of the chicken, vegetables and gravy was too much for standard 9 inch pie pan.

I made this and followed the recipe. It was excellent and my family loved it!!! The only thing was that it made so much I ended up putting the pie crust in a 9x13 glass dish and topping it with a couple of extra pie crust's that I had. Nothing went to waste..my family ate it all within a couple of days.

Very good for a traditional pot pie recipe ... simple to prepare (though you need to start a couple of hours prior to your meal). I made no modifications other than using half gravy mix, and half roux with chicken stock, and this turned out fine.
Keep the broth you heated the veggies in to use to make the gravy. Also, if you are lactose intolerant, use it in place of milk.

The recipe was great I first thought it was a lot of vegetables. But they tasted so good! I didn’t use premade pie crust. I made my own from a Pioneer Woman’s recipe. We will definitely make again. I’m thinking since there are just the two of us to make small individual pot pies next time. My husband loved this recipe. I did use leftover homemade gravy.

I read your comments that it could be also a chicken noodle base. So rather then draining the veggies, I took a slotted spoon to drain liquid in pan and left veggies and stock in container. I hate food and ingredients going to waste. I did not use the veggies you suggested. I cut 1/4 green cabbage, 3 carrots, 1 can strained NSA diced tomatoes, 3 celery, 6 shitake mushrooms, 8 baby bell mushrooms, 4 breasts of chicken breast I cooked in foil the night before. I used low sodium in ever ingredient except the pie crust. I also upped the garlic and added rosemary, oregano, Basil, and 5 cloves of fresh minced garlic to make up for no salt. I also only slightly covered the top of the pot pie with gravy as I felt putting the remaining would make pot pie too runny. I also used heavy whipping cream and egg wash as I was using up what I have. Both turned out amazing and it broke down to, 4 meals of chicken noodle with macaroni noodles. I added broth to 3 servings to stretch it to gift to others. The pot pie recipe I will do again. Ohh lastly I cooked bottom of pot pie pie crust for 8 minutes rather then putting it in raw and cooking all at once. I also took my pot pie out at 20 minutes as top was golden brown. This will definitely be a keeper and plan to just use what veggies I have on hand. Thank you for your recipe
I loved it! it was so easy and tasty!
It turned out pretty good but the filling and gravy was double the amount needed. Did anyone test this recipe before putting it on All Recipes?
My family loved it and my husband told me that his new favorite casserole

I took out the green beans and peas for more carrots and celery. Also tripled the broth and used it to make the gravy, no point in wasting it! It definitely adds a lot of flavor. I also season chicken breast ahead of time and let it marinate for at least a day then add it to the broth and veg to boil before shredding it. Definitely makes two 9in pies! I feel it’s too much work to make your own crust on top of everything else so I got store bought but definitely delicious either way.

As I learned long ago, recipes are just a guideline. I made a roux and sauteed the vegetables. I sauteed boneless skinless chicken breast and two tenders I had left over from Pretty Bird chicken. It came out very well and was devoured by my wife myself and our guests.
Delicious but too much work for me personally. I also struggled with dumping the chicken broth down the drain.. by the time you cook it with all those veggies you have soup 🤷🏻‍♀️
Absolutely delicious ❤️⭐️⭐️⭐️Thank You ⭐️⭐️⭐️
